Okay. Is NYC Aging considering an increase to meal reimbursement rates? If so, to what and when?

We do an analysis, which is how we've arrived at our rate increases in the past. We look at food costs, for Home-Delivered Meals, we look at gasoline, we look at a ratio of number of staff required to satisfy those number of meals, and then we can come up with a dollar amount for per meal cost.

For HDM, for example, we were able to successfully to work on getting the dollar increase, right from ’23 to ’24…
Sorry, on which increase?

HDM. So HDM went from $11.78 to $12.78. That was based on actually looking at the cost so we did that. Now, when we look at OACs, and we mentioned earlier, because there's so much underspending, that's how we, it's self-funded, those costs are being self-funded internally.
Okay.

We send out a survey, look at the cost. We go back and figure out what the total need is and then go from there. OACs, we've done the same thing but, unfortunately, because of the underspending in those areas, we don't actually get an increase in the meal cost but, again, a lot of it's self-funded.

We have a very robust nutritionist unit who works very closely with the OACs around nutritional services, both not only in the preparation of meals, in cost management
